transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Ice coming back this thickly within two weeks of a full defrost usually means moist air is getting into the freezer and freezing out. The most common cause is the door not sealing properly. It can turn into a vicious circle: ice builds up, the bottom drawer won't push home, the door then sits slightly open, and more ice forms. The likely causes, most likely first:
1. Door seal or door closing. A split, flattened or folded seal, a door that has dropped on its hinge, or the fridge freezer leaning forward so the door doesn't swing shut on its own.
2. A blocked defrost drain. Water can't get away and refreezes in the base, which pushes the bottom drawer out.
3. On a frost-free model only, a fault in the automatic defrost system (usually the defrost heater, defrost thermostat or the control that runs the defrost). That ices up the back panel rather than the front. Where the ice is building tells these apart. Two quick checks you can do now (no need to switch off):
1. Paper test. Close the freezer door on a sheet of paper at several points around the edge, especially at the bottom and on the handle side, and pull it out each time. If it slides out with no grip anywhere, the seal isn't sealing there. Also run your fingers round the seal and feel for splits or a section that has come away or folded.
2. Door and levelling. Make sure nothing is stopping the door, such as a drawer not pushed fully in or food sticking out. Open the door halfway and let go. It should swing shut on its own. If it doesn't, wind the front feet up a little so the unit tilts very slightly backwards. If the seal is torn or won't grip, a replacement door seal is the likely fix. If it's just dirty or folded, warm soapy water and easing it back into shape often sorts it. If the seal and door both look fine, the drain or the defrost system become the suspects, which is why I'm asking where the ice forms.

did paper test, slides straight out at the bottom corner, grips everywhere else. seal is split about 5cm at the bottom corner and the bit on the hinge side is flattened. ice is mostly round the front edge and bottom drawer, its level too

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
That pretty much settles it. A 5cm split right where the paper slides out, plus a flattened section on the hinge side, fits the pattern exactly. The unit is level, so the door seal is the culprit, and I'm fairly confident a replacement freezer door seal is the fix. A split can't be repaired, and once a seal has flattened it rarely recovers enough to grip properly. To find the right seal I'll need the model number. It's usually on a sticker inside the fridge, on a side wall near the salad drawer. It may be an Indesit code plus a separate service or product number, and both are worth sending. If you can't get to it right now, that can wait. 1. Knock back the worst of the ice around the bottom drawer, using warm water or another defrost rather than anything sharp, so the drawer can push fully home and the door closes squarely.
2. Make sure the bottom drawer is fully in every time you shut the door. A drawer sticking out will hold the door off the seal even after the new seal is fitted. Fitting a new seal is usually a manageable owner job. Most push into a channel in the door liner or sit under a few screws behind the lip. A new seal often comes folded and kinked, so a few minutes with a hairdryer on warm (not hot) helps it settle. If the ice still comes back quickly with a new seal fitted and gripping all round, the next suspect would be the defrost drain.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
model is IB55532W, its on the rating plate. indesit. what do i search for to get the seal?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Search for "Indesit IB55532W freezer door seal". Use the word "freezer", because the fridge and freezer doors usually take different-sized seals, and getting the wrong one is the most common mistake. I can't find a confirmed seal match for IB55532W in the catalogue I check, so I can't point you to a specific part. The safest way to get the right one: 1. Indesit's official spares site (or their customer service line) is the best route. Enter the model number, and also any service or product number printed on the same rating plate (often a shorter code near the model). Indesit sometimes made several versions under one model number, and that extra code is what pins down the correct seal.
2. If you buy from another spares retailer, only buy a seal they list against your exact model and that service code. Check that the listing says freezer door and that the dimensions match your current seal. You can measure the old seal's height and width across the door before ordering to double-check.
3. Avoid "universal" cut-to-fit seals. They rarely grip as well as the proper moulded one, and you'd be back to ice build-up. If the official site doesn't list a seal for your model, or it's no longer available, an Indesit or independent engineer can usually source and fit one. Ask about the cost first. On an older, cheaper fridge freezer, a seal plus a call-out can sometimes get close to the cost of a new machine, so that's worth weighing up. Until the new seal arrives, keep the bottom drawer pushed fully home and knock back the ice now and then so the door closes as well as it can.

candidates: Warm, damp air getting in past the freezer door seal or because the door isn't closing fully (seal, hinge or levelling) (high)
Blocked or frozen defrost drain letting water refreeze in the base, pushing the bottom drawer out (medium)
Automatic defrost system fault (only if it's a frost-free model) (low)
